label: Correspondent Banking Risk
description: Bank-side correspondent banking risk management: respondent risk rating, the Wolfsberg CBDD questionnaire, nested / downstream-clearing risk, transaction monitoring of correspondent flows, and exit / de-risking governance against AMLR Art. 36–39 and FATF R.13.

claudeKnowledge.description: AMLR (EU) 2024/1624 Art. 36–39 (Art. 36 cross-border correspondent EDD; Art. 38 third-country respondent measures; Art. 39 shell-institution prohibition); AMLD6 (EU) 2024/1640; FATF Recommendation 13 + Interpretive Note; Wolfsberg Correspondent Banking Due Diligence Questionnaire (CBDDQ) v1.4 (2023) and the Wolfsberg Correspondent Banking Principles; Wolfsberg/ICC/BAFT Trade Finance Principles; Basel Committee guidelines on sound management of ML/TF risks (Annex 2 — correspondent banking); FATF Guidance on Correspondent Banking Services (2016); FSB de-risking reports; EBA Guidelines on ML/TF risk factors (EBA/GL/2021/02) on correspondent relationships; TFR (EU) 2023/1113 for payment-message information.

guidedInputs.label: Known Issues, Red Flags, or Concerns
guidedInputs.description: Describe the respondent, observed flows, prior findings, or specific worries to focus the analysis. Include CBDDQ gaps, alert trends, or any negative news.
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. Respondent is a smaller bank in a FATF grey-list jurisdiction whose CBDDQ shows it does not screen its own downstream FIs; we have observed nested MSB flows it did not disclose; correspondent TM is generating round-amount, rapid-pass-through alerts to the same five beneficiary banks; last on-site visit was 2022...

exampleInput: We are the FCC / correspondent banking team at a Nordic universal bank (EUR-clearing correspondent for EEA and select EMEA respondents). We are running an event-driven review of a respondent bank in a FATF grey-list jurisdiction after our transaction-monitoring team flagged rising USD pass-through volumes to the same handful of beneficiary banks. The respondent's Wolfsberg CBDDQ (v1.4) is on file from 2023 but several AML-programme and downstream-clearing questions are answered 'partially' or left blank, and it has not disclosed whether it provides nested / downstream correspondent services to other FIs or MSBs. Produce a respondent risk re-rating, identify the nested / payable-through-account exposure and the correspondent-flow TM gaps, set out what additional information and CBDDQ clarifications we must obtain, and frame an exit-versus-remediate decision with the governance steps and FATF R.13 / AMLR Art. 36–39 basis. We do not want blanket de-risking — show the proportionate path.

exampleValues.known_concerns: Rising USD pass-through to five repeat beneficiary banks; CBDDQ (2023, v1.4) has blank downstream-clearing and AML-programme answers; respondent has not disclosed nested MSB / FI relationships; last on-site review 2022; correspondent TM only screens our respondent, not the underlying ordering/beneficiary parties in the MT202COV / pacs.009 cover chain.
